claims.statement: `packages/design-system` is the workspace package `@mcm/design-system`, a Material Design 3 token set plus Tamagui component library shared by the web and native builds of `frontend/mcm-app`. Its package exports are the barrel `.` → `index.ts` and `./tamagui.config` → `tamagui.config.ts`, and `expo`, `react` and `react-native` are declared as peer dependencies so the package never decides the app's framework versions.

Every semantic MD3 colour role is theme-split: `lightColors` and `darkColors` each map the tonal palettes to a distinct value per role (primary, secondary, tertiary, success, error, background/surface, surface1–surface5, outline, scrim, …), so one token resolves to an AA-passing colour on both the near-white light surface and the near-black dark surface.

The semantic colour roles exist only in the Tamagui themes, never also as colour tokens: the config flattens raw palette tones into tokens (`primaryP40`, …) but deliberately omits `...lightColors`, because Tamagui 3 resolves a bare name on a colour property token-first and theme second, so a duplicated light value would win inside the dark theme. Consumers read roles through `useTheme()` as `theme.<role>?.val`, and Tamagui 3 token/theme names carry no `$` sigil.

`success` is a first-class semantic colour role rather than an ad-hoc green literal, added so positive/verified state flows through the theme: positive text uses `theme.success?.val`, a filled verified banner uses `successContainer` with `onSuccessContainer`, and no consumer may use a green literal. The role exists in both colour maps and both themes, and the three required WCAG AA pairings are asserted in `components/success-token.test.tsx`.

The type scale is the MD3 step set `{11,12,14,16,18,22,24,28,32,36,45,57}`, with Outfit carrying display/headline/title and Inter carrying body/label. Both fonts declare only the faces 400/500/600/700, which is the rationale behind compliance rule R6: a `fontWeight` above 700 has no real face and is synthesized by the renderer.

`dark` is the recommended default theme, justified by the product being a movie-collection app where a home-theatre aesthetic is natural. The dark background is deliberately deeper than MD3's standard dark neutral — `#0F1117` instead of `#1A1C1E` — to evoke a cinema and make posters stand out.

Tamagui is pinned to one exact version (`3.0.18`) across both the design-system and mcm-app manifests, and `scripts/__tests__/tamagui-version-lockstep.guard.test.mjs` enforces that: no range specifiers, both manifests agreeing on the version, exactly one `@tamagui/core` and one `@tamagui/web` in the lock, no remaining `@tamagui/babel-plugin` in either manifest or `babel.config.js`, and every Tamagui update resolving to a single Renovate `tamagui` group so a partial lock refresh cannot split the set.

The app runs Tamagui runtime-only through `<TamaguiProvider>` with no Babel or Metro compiler plugin: Tamagui 3 removed the Babel plugin, and its replacement `@tamagui/metro-plugin` 3.0.x was measured and rejected because it lowered some web modules to static class names without emitting their CSS while saving no bytes. This is a measured decision, not a leftover, and re-adding a compiler incidentally is out of bounds.

Because Tamagui 3 removed config-level `defaultProps`, the body font and the theme's `onBackground` colour live on the design system's own `components/primitives/Text.tsx`. `components/text-defaults.test.tsx` pins that observable behaviour for both themes and fails if any source file outside `primitives/Text.tsx` imports `Text` from `@tamagui/core`, which would bypass the defaults (on native, leaving black text on the dark theme).

The app enforces design-system usage with a static scan run by its Jest unit suite, not a runtime check. The rules live in `frontend/mcm-app/tests/unit/design-system-compliance.test.ts` as one `it()` per rule (R1–R7), each asserting zero violations over `frontend/mcm-app/src/**` while excluding the `bff-server`/`bff-api`/`__mocks__`/`unit-tests` directories and test/spec files.

The scan engine lives in `frontend/mcm-app/tests/unit/ds-compliance-scan.ts`: it reads, neutralizes and brace-parses every source file once into a cached `ScanFile`, and the seven rule predicates iterate that cache. A failure reports `file:line — rule — snippet` per violation so a migration can be driven file by file, and the predicates are unit-tested in isolation on synthetic `ScanFile`s.

A deliberate deviation from a compliance rule requires BOTH a `// ds-exempt(R<n>): <reason>` marker on the flagged line or the immediately-preceding non-blank line (`ds-exempt(all)` exempts every rule) AND an entry in `specs/017-design-system-consistency/contracts/sanctioned-deviations.md`. The scan only sees the marker; the catalogue entry is the review-enforced half of the pair, and that contract file is the single source of truth for approved exceptions.

A change to the design system's type scale or loaded font weights breaks the compliance scan in the app repository, not in this package: the MD3 scale set and the 700 maximum-weight ceiling are constants declared inside the app's scan engine, so the app's unit suite turns red when those package properties move.

The orange (tertiary) usage cap — at most 3–4 elements per screen, with the Grumpy Robot avatar, rating stars, the single "Add movie" call-to-action and attention highlights such as a media/quality mismatch badge as the sanctioned uses — is a convention that the R1–R7 scan does not enforce, so over-using orange is a design regression that will not fail CI.

The design system's own Jest suite uses the `jest-expo` preset with `jest/tamagui-cjs-resolver.js`, which redirects the two Tamagui 3 subpaths whose `react-native` export condition is ESM-only `.mjs` to their CJS builds — a Jest-only problem, since Metro loads `.mjs` fine. `testMatch` covers the whole package rather than only `components/**`, so a new test directory cannot be silently invisible to the runner.

Beyond the rule table, the sanctioned-deviations contract also carries the R1 colour-utility allowlist and the intentional control conventions — two-tier destructive emphasis by surface density and single-select `Chip type="choice"` versus multi-select `Chip type="filter"` — which are documented deliberate differentiation rather than drift.

The orange call-to-action is `PillButton`, a dedicated primitive rather than a `Button` variant because its look sits between the MD3 Button sizes and is semantically singular, and the design system's `FAB` defaults to the tertiary colour scheme — together with `MovieCard`'s `FormatBadge` highlight, these are the sanctioned orange surfaces.
